judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are the identically printed CAPS bullet 'Reads aloud to a partner' under Reading and Phonics / Paired-Independent Reading, but they sit at different configured grade coordinates: second = Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 3; first = Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 4. This is a cross-grade CAPS recurrence rather than generic within-grade repetition: the bounded source context for the Grade 3 occurrence shows the same table row carrying markedly more demanding companion expectations (monitoring self for word recognition and comprehension, using self-correcting strategies, and reading independently at a more complex level), whereas the Grade 2 occurrence sits in a row framed by daily 20-minute paired reading practice alongside reading own and others' writing. Reading aloud to a partner on Grade 2 texts therefore develops the oral fluency and partner-reading routine that supports performing the same act on the longer, more complex Grade 3 Term 4 material with greater independence and self-monitoring. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (Grade 2 to Grade 3), the only permitted buildsTowards direction. Evidence limits noted: both endpoints' source evidence and supporting LC evidence are truncated (24 omitted source evidence items each) and the shared LC adds only wording-level overlap, so the complexity contrast is inferred from the available row-level context rather than full statement text; this limits but does not undermine confidence.

Nomination signals are weak (shared tokens limited to 'a' and 'for', rank gap 0, shared Grade ancestor only), so the symmetric, non-dependency reading is the defensible judgment. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (coordinate rank 0) and share the CAPS stem 'Distinguishes between the shapes of different letters and words', but the exemplification differs materially. The first (Grade R, Term 1, Emergent Reading / Emergent reading skills) operationalises the skill through general visual discrimination with non-print material: sorting objects that are the same, sequencing pictures, picking out the odd picture. The second (Grade R, Term 4, Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning) applies the same discrimination directly to print, sorting plastic letters into groups of the same letter. That is a Term 1 to Term 4 move within one grade, from generic shape/object discrimination to letter-specific discrimination, so proficiency in the earlier statement supports success in the later one; direction first_to_second is the permitted earlier-to-later direction. Noted limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, but the retained statement text, Term and Skill Area scopes are sufficient for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Listening and Speaking (Oral) under the same 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' sub-strand, and both explicitly concern imaginative use of language in playful oral forms. The second SFI (Grade 1, Term 4, rank 1) has learners listening to, enjoying and responding to picture/word puzzles, riddles and jokes 'using language imaginatively' - a receptive and responsive engagement with playful, rhyme-and-wordplay language. The first SFI (Grade 2, Term 2, rank 2) requires learners to compose their own rhymes using imaginative language, i.e. independent production rather than response. Experience in enjoying and responding to oral wordplay plausibly supports success in generating original rhymes, and the direction lower-to-higher grade matches the permitted second_to_first direction. This is a curriculum-inferred developmental link, not an asserted prerequisite; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream audit/merge context, which limits certainty but does not conflict with the Term/Grade/Skill Area evidence used.
